title: Product Growth Glossary: Metrics Defined and Benchmarked
meta_description: Twenty-five growth and monetisation metrics, each with its formula, its denominator and the published range, so you know which definition you are reading.

visuals.alt: Six reference points showing how wide the published spread is on metrics people quote as single numbers: the freemium conversion distribution, the free-trial conversion distribution, the activation median against its top and bottom quartiles, the mobile lifetime-value to acquisition-cost band, onboarding tour completion across 464 companies with its interquartile range, and checklist completion at two different lengths, each row carrying its source and verification date
visuals.caption: Why a single benchmark number rarely settles anything. Verified 30 September 2026.

faq.q: Why does every entry give a range rather than one number?
faq.a: Because the published spreads are wide enough that a single figure misleads. Activation has a median of 41.7%, a top quartile of 71% and a bottom quartile of 19%. A product at 30% is below median and above the bottom quartile, and only the range tells you that.

faq.q: How do I know which definition of a metric I am reading?
faq.a: Check the denominator. Most disagreements about a metric are disagreements about what goes underneath the line: ARPU over all users or over payers, retention over installs or over activated users, churn over accounts or over revenue. Each entry here names its denominator first.

faq.q: Are these definitions the same as my analytics tool's?
faq.a: Often not, and that is the point of reading the formula rather than the name. A tool reports what it can compute from the events it receives, which is not always the definition the benchmark was built on.

faq.q: Why do step counts change a completion rate so much?
faq.a: Because each step is a chance to leave. Checklists of three to five steps complete at 67%, against 18% for ten steps or more. The content did not get worse; there was simply more of it to abandon.

unique_value_statement: Each entry leads with the denominator rather than the name, and gives the published distribution rather than a median, because the common failure is two teams comparing numbers that were never the same measurement.
